acceptance: finish accepts an optional closing note stored on the item detail in the same state commit as status done, with a size limit of at least 4,000 characters and the same control-character rules as drop_reason; a test asserts one commit
A publication retry after a competing push stores the note once
show_item and todo-db show return the note; list_items rows are unchanged
The tool schema snapshot, instructions, README and CHANGELOG are updated; the catalog todo skill tells agents to pass the note to finish instead of a separate context_append once a release carries it
context: Found 2026-10-31 by the review of the BenchBox drop-reason item and again while closing items on 2026-11-01.
description: finish(id, generation, final_evidence) accepts only prepared-batch final evidence, so agents record what closed an item with a separate update_item context_append and then finish: two state commits per close. Every close in the BenchBox and benchbox-site trackers on 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-01 followed that pattern (about 15 items), and the site-split-99-closeout close did too (af92ea1bea then b236b81d18 in the BenchBox tracker). The failure modes match the ones drop had before 0.12.0: if the finish fails after the note, the item stays open with a note saying it closed; a re-run duplicates the note; nothing ties the note to the close. Closing notes in practice run 500-1,500 characters across lines.
